entries.title: Pentagonal Lattice Geometry
entries.description: A multi-sheeted covering construction in which the regular pentagon develops fractional dimension (d ≈ 2.37) and spinor-like holonomy — a discrete model where a single loop requires two passes to return to identity.
entries.launchLabel: Open the Pentagonal Lattice Geometry lab

entries.title: Quadratic Quasi-Newton
entries.description: A new optimization algorithm for smooth functions that interpolates between gradient descent and L-BFGS along a quadratic path, with a provable descent guarantee and no extra hyperparameters.
entries.author: SimiaCryptus

seo.title: QQN Optimizer — Quadratic-Quasi-Newton, Illustrated
seo.description: An illustrated, interactive introduction to the QQN (Quadratic-Quasi-Newton) optimizer: the quadratic path between gradient descent and quasi-Newton, its four strategy slots, what makes it different, and its history.

entries.subtitle: Standalone · optimization

entries.title: PID-Regulated Cellular Automaton
entries.description: A cellular automaton whose update rule is a per-cell PID controller: each cell measures its active-neighbor count against a target and computes proportional, integral, and derivative terms to decide its next state. The result is a rule family with local memory (integral windup), local anticipation (derivative), and tunable dynamical regimes — under-damped ripples, critically-damped blobs, over-damped glassy creep — all from the same control-theoretic mechanism. Swap the domain for an excitable bioelectrical membrane (spiking, refractoriness, propagating waves) or for Dither-CA, where each cell regulates its neighbourhood's mean colour toward a target image.

seo.launchLabel: Open the PID-Regulated Cellular Automaton lab

entries.title: Which Direction? → Where on the Curve?
entries.description: An interactive, scroll-driven tutorial on the Quadratic Quasi-Newton (QQN) optimizer. Reframes optimization from "which direction should I move?" into "where on this curve should I stop?" — with live contour maps, deformable search curves, and a four-axis factoring that collapses a zoo of classical methods (gradient descent, momentum, L-BFGS, trust regions, OWL-QN) into points in one configuration space. Built to make the geometry something you can feel, not just read.
entries.subtitle: Interactive · optimization

entries.title: Geometric Entropy Lab
entries.description: A continuous analogue of the Erdős distinct-distance problem. Points on a manifold are arranged to extremize the Shannon entropy of their pairwise-distance distribution.

entries.title: RCC — Rational Certificate Complexity
entries.description: Treats every convergence sequence as a rational certificate engine, measures certificate bit-length against demanded tolerance ε, and stratifies mathematical constants into cost classes RC₁/RC₂/RC₃.
entries.subtitle: Trilogy I · the foundational vocabulary
entries.pitch: The foundation of the trilogy. Treats every convergence sequence as a rational certificate engine, measures its bit-length versus demanded tolerance ε, and stratifies constants into cost classes (RC₁/RC₂/RC₃). Establishes the regularity condition, a Θ(log 1/ε) lower bound, and the central separation algebraic irrationals vs. π and e. It fixes the vocabulary the other two essays invoke.

entries.title: Irrational Lattice
entries.description: A new primitive: deterministic, algebraic “colored noise” for lattices. Coordinates in ℚ(√D) deform ℤᵈ and snap back via a nearest-lattice map — provably aperiodic, spectrally tunable, integer-arithmetic clean.

entries.title: PI_RCC — The Simplest Increment: x + sin(x)
entries.description: A cubic-convergent iteration for π whose outer recurrence is not hypergeometric — it falls outside RCC's classified class, yet still attains optimal RC₁ certificate cost. Develops derivative engineering (g(α)=0, g′(α)=−1, g″(α)=0) and the tower of continua from ℚ through algebraic, analytic, elliptic/modular constants and periods.
entries.subtitle: Trilogy II · stress-testing the boundary
entries.pitch: A cubic-convergent iteration for π whose outer recurrence is not hypergeometric — it falls outside RCC's classified class, yet still attains optimal RC₁ cost. Develops derivative engineering and the tower of continua (ℚ → algebraic → analytic → elliptic/modular → periods). Where RCC defines the cost classes, PI_RCC shows their boundary is permeable.

entries.title: NAM — Numbers as Machines
entries.description: Trilogy III · the executable substrate. A generator-based numerics library where every number is a forkable, deterministic nano-VM emitting an infinite digit stream: a two-tier ABI, signed-digit arithmetic, base-as-codec, p-adics as periodic automata, BBP skip-ahead, and an interval-honest account of equality.
entries.subtitle: Trilogy III · the executable substrate
entries.pitch: A generator-based numerics library where every number is a forkable, deterministic nano-VM emitting an infinite digit stream. RCC's cost classes resurface here as generator state-dimension tiers, with a two-tier ABI, base-as-codec, BBP-as-resonance, and an honest interval account of equality. Where RCC measures and PI_RCC engineers, NAM builds the machine that runs them all.

entries.title: Spacelike Knots
entries.description: A knot equipped with a Minkowski metric, turning crossings into causal inversions. The distance matrix becomes a causal diagram: timelike, spacelike, and null separations color-coded across the whole knot.

entries.title: Magnet Lattice
entries.description: Explore the dynamics of re-rotating magnets and their emergent behaviors.
entries.pitch: Explore the dynamics of re-rotating magnets and their emergent behaviors.

entries.title: The Extension Ladder: One Way to Watch Number Systems Grow
entries.description: A logical reconstruction of the generative mechanism behind number systems: exploit a structure's affordances, force an element outside the set, extend, and repeat — from the integers up through the complex plane, with side branches into modular arithmetic, wavelets, and the p-adics.

entries.title: Theme CAD
entries.description: A theme designer for PointCAD, allowing you to create and customize themes for your CAD projects.

entries.title: Pastaponics
entries.description: A modular, 3D‑printed hydroponic medium enabling plant‑driven nutrient self‑regulation through spatially differentiated nutrient channels.

entries.title: Layered Cellular Automata
entries.description: Langton's ants write a colored substrate that gates where Conway's Life is allowed to live. Three feedback layers — ants → substrate → life → substrate → ants — produce highways, colonies, and fractal boundaries. For a playable take on Conway's Life and 50+ other rulesets, see the sister site The Arcade of Life at https://aol.cognotik.com/

entries.title: Space-Color Symmetry
entries.description: A pixel canvas where symmetry doesn't just mirror your strokes — it rewires the diffusion graph. Heat flows along symmetry orbits, producing kaleidoscope dynamics on a quotient-like manifold.

entries.title: Basic Math Experiments
entries.description: A set of interactive browser experiments: the Mandelbrot set, the Sieve of Eratosthenes, Fourier series epicycles, and the Collatz conjecture.
entries.author: Fun With Math

seo.title: Basic Math Experiments – Fun With Math
seo.description: Explore the Mandelbrot set, prime sieves, Fourier series and the Collatz conjecture in interactive, no-install browser demos.

pages.title: Mandelbrot Set – Fun With Math
pages.description: Explore the Mandelbrot Set fractal interactively in your browser.

pages.title: Prime Number Sieve – Fun With Math
pages.description: Watch the Sieve of Eratosthenes find primes interactively.

pages.title: Fourier Series – Fun With Math
pages.description: Visualize Fourier series approximations with interactive spinning circles.

pages.title: Collatz Conjecture – Fun With Math
pages.description: Explore the Collatz Conjecture: the 3n+1 problem visualized.

entries.title: Bidirectional Markov Text Analyzer
entries.description: Build a language model from your own corpus, then watch another text light up token-by-token by how surprising it is. Forward and backward order-n Markov models are merged into a single surprise heatmap, with click-to-replace predictions, add-k smoothing, backoff, and live perplexity.

entries.title: Chaos Garden
entries.description: An in-browser, gamified fluid dynamics simulation: paint banks and obstacles into a channel, then watch the water braid, eddy and refuse to repeat itself.

entries.title: Static Secrets
entries.description: Publish encrypted content anywhere and decrypt it entirely in your browser. The host serves opaque bytes; only you hold the key.

entries.title: Relativistic 2-Body Gravity
entries.description: A 2-body gravitational system with relativistic adjustments and time-delayed (retarded) interactions. Gravity propagates at finite speed c, breaking Newton's third law and producing orbital precession, frame-dragging analogues, and chaotic orbits.

entries.title: Constrained Mesh Enclosure Lab
entries.description: A deformable surface mesh flows downhill on geometric fitness functionals (area, volume, edge-length entropy, angular regularity, Laplacian smoothness) while an exact continuous collision-detection pipeline guarantees it never intrudes into an inner keep-out volume — a differentiable shrink-wrap where every gradient step is clipped at the moment of contact.
entries.launchLabel: Open the Constrained Mesh Enclosure Lab

entries.title: The Prime Sieve as a Stack of Orthogonal Periodic Fields
entries.description: An interactive essay on the periodic machinery underneath the primes: each prime emits an orthogonal exclusion field, their stacked product has primorial period, and CRT independence makes density multiplicative, entropy additive, and spectral support disjoint.

entries.title: Fractal Mosaic
entries.description: A recursive photomosaic viewer: an infinite, self-similar plane where every photo dissolves into a mosaic of other photos from your album, forever.

entries.title: Point CAD
entries.pitch: A point-based CAD system for designing complex geometries.

entries.title: Optimization Mechanics Visualizer
entries.description: Drop GD, Adam, L-BFGS, and QQN onto the same rugged 2D loss landscape and watch, step by step, how each finds its way downhill. Configurable terrain (slopes, bowls, high-frequency noise, confounding lattices), a fading path with live gradient arrows, and projected statistics bars that expose the running gradient and squared-gradient accumulations adaptive optimizers quietly maintain. Step through QQN's oracle point, quadratic path, and line-search probes to see the mechanics papers describe in equations.

entries.title: nam — Numbers as Machines
entries.description: A calculator where every number is a deterministic, forkable virtual machine emitting an infinite digit stream on demand. Comparison is honestly tri-state, fork cost is annotated by tier, and unprovable digits render as 'pending (null)' rather than a comfortable lie.

entries.title: No-Three-in-Line: A Visual Theory Explorer
entries.description: An infinite-canvas explorer for the no-three-in-line rule under deterministic greedy growth: ring-major Chebyshev (L∞) traversal, forced empty strips, finite-horizon collinearity, centered-window density fields, top-K certified windows, paranoid verification and one-click export.

entries.title: No-Three-in-Line Lab
entries.description: A live, physics-flavored playground for the classic no-three-in-line problem: place as many points as possible on an n×n grid so that no three are ever collinear. Instead of searching discrete arrangements, the lab relaxes the lattice constraint and lets points drift under an energy landscape — a magnetic pull toward integer positions, a repulsive force that builds as any triple flattens toward a line, and optional spacing and entropic-noise terms. Gradient optimizers (Adam, SGD+momentum, L-BFGS, QQN) roll the configuration downhill while tracked lines are tinted by population (blue under-filled, green exactly two, red over-crowded). Tune the forces mid-run, drag points by hand, restart for a fresh seed, or switch to 3D mode and orbit a cubic lattice.

entries.title: Dihedral Attractors
entries.description: Rung 4 of the geometric-energy ladder: sculpt meshes by optimizing functionals over triangulation dihedral angles — flatness, uniform folds, creasing, smoothness, or fold entropy — with points free or pinned to a sphere, torus, or saddle.

seo.title: Dihedral Attractors — Sculpting Geometry by Optimizing Fold Angles
seo.description: An interactive lab that minimizes or maximizes energies built from the dihedral angles of a live triangulation, coaxing point clouds into folded, curvature-defined attractors reminiscent of the Platonic solids.

entries.title: Fitting Point Clouds with Iterated Transforms
entries.description: An interactive TensorFlow.js lab that reverse-engineers an iterated function system from a target point cloud: a handful of affine transforms are enumerated to a fixed depth (commutative multisets via binary powers, or ordered words) and tuned by gradient descent against a symmetric Chamfer loss. Draw or load a target shape, pick the number of transforms and the depth, and watch a random constellation self-organize into the outline you asked for.

entries.title: Geometric Entropy Lab — No-Three-in-Line
entries.description: A continuous relaxation of the no-three-in-line problem: line-centered potential wells with a non-monotonic population-fitness response f(p) = (p - 2)^2 attract points until a line holds two and repel once it holds three. Annealed Gaussian well width, a cosine lattice-snapping potential and TensorFlow.js optimizers (SGD / Adam / L-BFGS) crystallize points onto the n x n grid, with discrete integer verification of every configuration.
entries.author: Wesley Roberts

seo.title: Geometric Entropy Lab: Entropic Search for the No-Three-in-Line Problem
seo.description: Interactive TensorFlow.js lab relaxing the no-three-in-line problem into a differentiable potential landscape, using population-fitness wells, annealed sigma schedules and lattice snapping to search for 2n-point grid configurations.

entries.title: Laser-Damage Camera Correction
entries.description: An offline, installable PWA that profiles a camera sensor to find dead, stuck, hot and noisy pixels — including whole laser-burn patches — then infills the damage from healthy neighbours so a wounded sensor keeps taking clean photos. Everything runs on-device; no frame ever leaves the browser.
entries.author: Nick Sullivan

seo.title: Laser-Damage Camera Correction — Profile and Repair a Damaged Sensor In-Browser
seo.description: Profile your camera to map dead, stuck and hot pixels, then automatically infill the damage from healthy neighbours. A privacy-preserving, offline-capable PWA for laser-damaged and hot-pixel-afflicted sensors.

entries.title: QQN — Quadratic Quasi-Newton (JAX/Optax)
entries.description: A pluggable JAX/Optax optimizer that blends steepest descent with a quasi-Newton oracle along a smooth quadratic path d(t) = t(1-t)(-∇f) + t²(-H∇f), letting a single line search pick the blend. No learning rate to tune. Factors optimization into four swappable axes — gradient, oracle, search, region — so L-BFGS, Newton, momentum, Barzilai-Borwein, Anderson, trust-region, OWL-QN and projected gradient all emerge as configurations.

seo.title: QQN: Quadratic Quasi-Newton Optimizer for JAX
seo.description: QQN interpolates gradient descent and L-BFGS along a quadratic path, discovering the right first-/second-order blend each iteration with no learning rate to tune. Pure-functional JAX: composes with jit, vmap, pmap and grad.
